title: Acts — A Replacement Time Someone Can Book, Versus One They Cannot
note: The single most confusable pair in the scheduling family, and the distinction is operational rather than linguistic: can the counterparty's agent complete a booking from this message ALONE? A counter-proposal names a slot the sender will honor, so accepting it closes the commitment with no further exchange — one message, one round trip saved. Availability describes windows that are not offers, so the counterparty must still propose, and an agent that treats the two alike will either book a slot nobody offered or waste a round trip re-asking for a time already on the table. Both refuse the original proposal, which is why a classifier keying on refusal alone gets this wrong; the discriminator is bindability, not sentiment.
